Jordan —

Legal confirms the short answers below; feel free to paste into a reply to Anna but attach the redline and the current subprocessors CSV. Suggested language (keeps to CPRA/CCPA bright-line):

• Role: "Redwood Inference will act as a Service Provider (as defined under the CCPA/CPRA) and, to the extent applicable under other U.S. state privacy laws, as a Processor. Redwood will process personal information only on behalf of and per the documented instructions of the controller and will not sell personal information."

• Transit encryption artifact: "Redwood secures in-transit data using TLS 1.2+ (we recommend TLS 1.3), employing AES-256 or equivalent ciphers for session encryption; TLS termination is performed at our customer-facing edge and keys are managed in our KMS. Customers can request architecture diagrams under an NDA if needed."

• Subprocessor notice: "We publish an up-to-date list of subprocessors and provide at least 30 days' notice prior to onboarding subprocessors that will process Personal Information. For emergency or critical security patches where a subprocessor must be engaged immediately, Redwood will provide post-onboard notice and elevated escalation/mitigation support."

Onshore fallback: we can provide an onshore-fallback plan for critical telemetry and customer-request routing, but that requires a Dedicated/Private deployment or a contractual commitment (reserved capacity) — we shouldn't promise it for the hosted plan.

I'll attach the redline DPA and the subprocessors manifest. Let me know if MedSecure asks for encryption certs or packet traces — we should push to provide certificate/KMS attestations under an SCP/NDA rather than live traces.

-Karthik
VP Legal & Policy | Redwood Inference
